name: Google Pay for the web
plain: Pays with a Google Pay card through a Google button or Payment Request.
meaning: Returns a tokenized card to the merchant's PSP after the person approves.

access.prompt_ui: Google Pay sheet with card selection
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Pays with a Google Pay card through a Google button or Payment Request.

limits.headline: Can start a Google Pay payment that you pick a card for and approve
limits.user_action: You tap the Google Pay button at checkout and pick a card.
can: Show the Google Pay sheet with your saved cards and addresses
Send the store a one time payment code once you approve
Share your name, email or address if you allow it
cannot: See your real card number in most set ups
Pay without you picking a card and approving
Use a card you did not choose to save
Keep a payment going after you close the sheet

story.what_it_is: Pay with a card saved in your Google account in one tap.

marketing.name: Google Pay API for the web
marketing.pitch: Google says the Google Pay API lets customers pay with cards saved to their Google Account.

story.for_you: You tap a Google Pay button, pick a card and confirm. The shop gets a secure token and does not see your full card number.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to cut checkout steps and card typing, which lifts sales. It works across browsers, not just Chrome.

use_cases.example: You buy a gift on a retail site in two taps.
A food order site finishes checkout with Google Pay.
A booking site fills your saved card and address in one step.
A web game store buys gems with Google Pay.
A streaming site signs you up for a plan in one tap.
A fraud team gets tokenized cards that are harder to steal.

technical_bounds: Needs Google account and saved card
Merchant must be approved by Google

history.change: Google Pay API for web launches
